draft.title: Judging how well a structure works
card: A text has a purpose, such as to persuade, inform or entertain. Its structure is the order of its parts. Its language features are the word choices and techniques it uses.
To judge a structure, first name the purpose. Then ask whether the order of the parts and the language help the text achieve it.

In an argument, a strong order might open with a clear claim, build with evidence, deal with an opposing view and end on the strongest point. If the best point comes first and the rest are weaker, the ending may feel flat.
A judgement needs evidence from the text. Say what the writer did, then explain how it helped or hindered the purpose.
draft.remember: Name the purpose first, then judge whether the order and language achieve it.

a.q: What should a reader do first when judging how well a text's structure works?
opts: Identify the purpose the text is trying to achieve
Count how many paragraphs the text has
List every technique the writer has used
Decide whether they agree with the writer
a.why: A structure can only be judged against what the text is trying to do, so the purpose comes first. Listing techniques is useful later, but it does not show whether they work.
a.clue: You need a goal before you can say if it was reached.

b.q: Sam writes a speech urging students to join a beach clean-up. It opens with the weakest reason, then gives a stronger one, and ends with a joke. Which judgement is best?
opts: The ending weakens the purpose, as it gives no push to act
The structure works, as a joke leaves a good impression
The structure works, as it has an opening and an ending
The speech fails, as a persuasive speech cannot be funny
b.why: The purpose is to persuade students to act, and ending on a joke gives no strong final push. Having an opening and an ending is not enough, because the judgement depends on whether the order serves the purpose.
b.clue: Ask what the last thing the audience hears does for the purpose.

a.best: Identify the purpose the text is trying to achieve

b.best: The ending weakens the purpose, as it gives no push to act
